newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar volatility beneficial - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar volatility beneficial - central bank.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Wednesday that recent volatility in the foreign exchange market after months of listless trade was both normal and beneficial.
"Today's inward and outward remittances were normal. There were no abnormal expectations," said Tuan Chin-sheng, deputy director general of the central bank's foreign exchange deparment.
"Today's movement was helpful for increasing market activity and enlarging the market scale," Tuan said.

Active U.S. dollar selling pushed the Taiwan dollar up sharply to a seven month high of T$27.382 on Wednesday in relatively volatile, high-turnover trade. Dealers said the trend was likely to continue ahead of the February 7 lunar new year holiday, traditionally a period of high currency demand.
"The central bank is watching the situation but will fully respect market forces," Tuan said. "Under reasonable conditions it is not necessary for the central bank to intervene."
Tuan did not define what he meant by reasonable conditions.
Tuan said the bank had not intervened on Wednesday.
Dealers have been expecting a Taiwan dollar appreciation in advance of the lunar new year and have said investors were awaiting signals as to how the central bank would respond.
The bank has consistently stood by what it calls its "stable to loose" monetary policy, hoping to accelerate what has been a disappointingly slow recovery without fuelling inflation.
